title: Repair Admin Battle matches list query

spec.problem: Admin Battle match actions accept roleless Admin sessions and silently ignore persistence failures: abort uses nonexistent updated_at while writing audit; rerun inserts nonexistent created_at/updated_at and also ignores audit errors.

acceptance.text: GET /api/admin/battle/matches returns a complete, ordered JSON list using the canonical started_at timestamp; anonymous access is rejected and roleless Admin read access remains allowed.

List and detail DTOs match BattleMatchesClient: list includes currentRoundIndex and _count.rounds; detail includes summary, ordered round rows and audit array using only columns that exist in the canonical schema.

Abort and rerun require battle.manage server-side and persist their state/audit atomically using only canonical battle_session columns; authorized UI mutations return the resulting detail while unauthorized Admins have no side effects.
Abort and rerun require battle.manage; invalid and unauthorized actions make no database changes.
Abort persists abandoned status and audit atomically using canonical battle_session columns.
Rerun creates a new in_progress session and audit atomically using canonical battle_session columns.
GET /api/admin/battle/system-parameters matches persisted database counts and returns 500 when any aggregate query fails.

spec.expected_behavior: Only Admins with battle.manage can abort/rerun. Valid abort persists abandoned status/reason/completion and one audit row; rerun persists a new in-progress session and one source audit row; invalid or unauthorized requests make no changes.
spec.observed_behavior: Visible abort on a disposable match returned success and wrote an audit event, but PostgreSQL still showed in_progress with no abandoned_reason because the handler ignored an update failure on nonexistent updated_at.
spec.rollback_plan: Revert the handler and its focused regression test; no database schema change or production data mutation.
